searchText: This is the contract address at etherscan.io not that it matters, but there is a warning sign on the contract tab it's been formally verified, even if there is a compiler bug, it's still formally shown to be safe. Sure, but I'm referring to the fact that the warning is there for everyone to see. Most people won't even know what a formal proof is. That warning doesn't help. <@!203220829473996800> does anyone know what these warnings mean as far as implications? can this be exploited in any way? how was it shown to be safe enough that one wouldn't worry about it being exploited in any way? i don't know if you can speak about the clients, but is this new money into ethereum or old money that's been sitting on the side as ETH coins already? (totally understand if you can't share, and apologize if it seems invasive) its pure curiosity super interesting question what a wonderful day for the deposit contract! 86K wohoo! officially broke the 5 digits remaining validators required for genesis 🙂 I have forgotten the answer: a new eth2 node can always be added by depositing 32 ETH, right? Even after launch. **vbuterin** yes
